import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_3.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source5_4_0", "Source5_4_1"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
df_01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="Artist", how="left")

# 2) JOIN : [["Source5_4_0", "Source5_4_3"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
df_013 = pd.merge(df_01, df3, on="Artist", how="left")

# 3) JOIN : [["Source5_4_2", "Source5_4_1"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
df_21 = pd.merge(df2, df1, on="Artist", how="left")

# Now join the two intermediate results on Artist to combine all data
# Because df_013 and df_21 both have 'Artist' and overlapping columns,
# but df_21 has Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated which are also in df_013,
# we need to decide how to combine them.

# The target schema columns are:
# ['Artist': string,
#  'Year Inducted': float,
#  'Years Waited': integer,
#  '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Inducted By': string,
#  'Influenced': integer,
#  'Certified Units (Millions)': float]

# df_013 has: Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Inducted By, Influenced, Certified Units (Millions)
# df_21 has: Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Influenced

# We want to combine these two on Artist, preferring non-null values from df_013,
# but filling missing values from df_21 where df_013 is null.

# Merge df_013 and df_21 on Artist with suffixes to distinguish columns
df_final = pd.merge(df_013, df_21, on="Artist", how="outer", suffixes=('_013', '_21'))

# For each column in target except Artist, pick values from df_013 if present, else from df_21

def coalesce(col1, col2):
    return col1.combine_first(col2)

# Year Inducted: float
df_final['Year Inducted'] = coalesce(df_final['Year Inducted_013'], df_final['Year Inducted_21'])

# Years Waited: integer (but source may have it as int or str, convert carefully)
# Convert to numeric with errors='coerce' to handle any non-numeric gracefully
df_final['Years Waited'] = coalesce(
    pd.to_numeric(df_final['Years Waited_013'], errors='coerce'),
    pd.to_numeric(df_final['Years Waited_21'], errors='coerce')
).round().astype('Int64')  # Use pandas nullable integer type

# # of Years Nominated: integer
df_final['# of Years Nominated'] = coalesce(
    pd.to_numeric(df_final['# of Years Nominated_013'], errors='coerce'),
    pd.to_numeric(df_final['# of Years Nominated_21'], errors='coerce')
).round().astype('Int64')

# Inducted By: string (only in df_013)
df_final['Inducted By'] = df_final['Inducted By']

# Influenced: integer
df_final['Influenced'] = coalesce(
    pd.to_numeric(df_final['Influenced_013'], errors='coerce'),
    pd.to_numeric(df_final['Influenced_21'], errors='coerce')
).round().astype('Int64')

# Certified Units (Millions): float (only in df_013)
df_final['Certified Units (Millions)'] = pd.to_numeric(df_final['Certified Units (Millions)'], errors='coerce')

# Artist: string
df_final['Artist'] = df_final['Artist']

# Select and reorder columns as per target schema
target_columns = [
    'Artist',
    'Year Inducted',
    'Years Waited',
    '# of Years Nominated',
    'Inducted By',
    'Influenced',
    'Certified Units (Millions)'
]

df_target = df_final[target_columns]

# Ensure data types match target schema exactly:
# Artist: string (object)
df_target['Artist'] = df_target['Artist'].astype(str)

# Year Inducted: float
df_target['Year Inducted'] = pd.to_numeric(df_target['Year Inducted'], errors='coerce')

# Years Waited: integer nullable
df_target['Years Waited'] = df_target['Years Waited'].astype('Int64')

# # of Years Nominated: integer nullable
df_target['# of Years Nominated'] = df_target['# of Years Nominated'].astype('Int64')

# Inducted By: string, keep NaN as is
df_target['Inducted By'] = df_target['Inducted By'].astype('string')

# Influenced: integer nullable
df_target['Influenced'] = df_target['Influenced'].astype('Int64')

# Certified Units (Millions): float
df_target['Certified Units (Millions)'] = pd.to_numeric(df_target['Certified Units (Millions)'], errors='coerce')

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read sources with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# UNION Source5_4_0 and Source5_4_2 (same schema except Source5_4_2 has NaNs)
union_0_2 = pd.concat([source0, source2], ignore_index=True)

# JOIN union_0_2 with Source5_4_1 on Artist
join_0_2_1 = pd.merge(union_0_2, source1, on="Artist", how="inner")

# JOIN the above result with Source5_4_3 on Artist
final_join = pd.merge(join_0_2_1, source3, on="Artist", how="inner")

# GROUP BY the leftmost non-float columns of target schema:
# ['Artist': string, 'Year Inducted': float, 'Years Waited': integer, '# of Years Nominated': integer, 'Inducted By': string]
# Aggregate Influenced and Certified Units (Millions) by max to remove duplicates
grouped = final_join.groupby(
    ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Inducted By'],
    as_index=False
).agg({
    'Influenced': 'max',
    'Certified Units (Millions)': 'max'
})

# Ensure columns are in the exact order as target schema
grouped = grouped[['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Inducted By', 'Influenced', 'Certified Units (Millions)']]

# Write output
grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_4/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
